mine: the way of the treacherous is their ruin
note: MT 'eytan means "enduring, perennial", which hardly fits; I follow the common emendation 'eydam "their calamity" (cf. LXX "in destruction"). The KJV's "hard" stretches 'eytan.

kjv: there is [that is] destroyed for want of judgment
mine: it (the fallow ground of the poor) is swept away through injustice
note: Hebrew belo' mishpat means "without justice": the poor lose their produce through injustice, not through their own lack of good judgment.
